options: Community participation is discouraged in a democracy
It helps build and support a healthy, functioning community
It has no benefit to the community at all
Only elected officials should participate in community life

questions.q: What term describes the right of citizens to elect representatives to make decisions on their behalf?
options: The right to own property only
The right to travel freely only

questions.q: What is one example of a responsibility shared by all members of a community, regardless of citizenship status?
options: Refusing to follow any local rules

questions.q: What term describes the process by which an immigrant becomes an official citizen of a new country?
Why might active citizenship, such as volunteering, benefit a community?
options: Only government workers should help their communities
It helps address local needs and strengthens community connections
It has no measurable impact on a community

questions.q: What term describes equal treatment and protection under the law for all individuals?
What responsibility do citizens typically have regarding paying for public services, such as roads and schools?
options: Only wealthy citizens are expected to pay taxes
Refusing to contribute to any public service
Paying taxes to help fund public services
Public services require no funding at all

questions.q: How can citizens participate in shaping government decisions beyond voting in elections?
options: Citizens are legally prevented from expressing opinions
Citizens have no ability to influence government decisions
By contacting representatives, attending meetings, and advocating for causes
Only elected officials can influence government decisions

questions.q: What term describes the protection of an individuals personal information and freedom from unreasonable interference?
options: A government requirement only for officials

questions.q: Why is understanding rights and responsibilities important for young people preparing to become active citizens?
options: Rights and responsibilities only apply to adults over 65
It has no relevance to their future participation in society
Only elected officials need to understand these concepts
It helps them participate thoughtfully and responsibly in society
